name: Oracle first-review held-out scenarios
scope: Fictional decision-time market evidence. This small, manually specified software/evidence-quality benchmark does not validate predictive edge, profitability, or professional competence.
caseSelection: Initial scenarios were specified from the approved requirements before reading the reviewer implementation. Additional adversarial regression cases were added during code review, and some failures informed fixes; this corpus is therefore a development evaluation set, not an untouched statistical holdout. A separate reserved set evaluates the frozen implementation. Arithmetic has objective answers; qualitative labels test only the disclosed structured method.

cases.purpose: A coherent long continuation paper idea can be supported when observed prices, declared horizon, invalidation and known risk inputs fit.
A coherent short idea receives the same treatment; support cannot be hard-wired to bullish markets.
A defined observation-to-revisit decision is valid without a position size, quote, or execution cost estimate.
A coherent thesis cannot waive an available configured risk cap.
Known transaction costs must be included when checking a plan close to its risk budget.
A long plan with its stop above the entry has inconsistent loss arithmetic.
The mirrored short stop defect must also be rejected.
A stop which exits before the learner's stated invalidation does not implement that thesis.
A long continuation hypothesis invalidated by a closed bar above the entry contradicts the selected loss-side condition.
A claimed long profit target below the entry is inconsistent even when reward/risk prose sounds reassuring.
A numerical stop alone does not explain what evidence would challenge the thesis.
The same long short-horizon evidence needs a contextual warning when the stated method requires agreement with a declining higher horizon.
A declared bounded countertrend method is not automatically defective merely because higher-horizon prices decline.
A handful of selected-timeframe bars cannot stand in for the required closed-bar history.
Missing higher-horizon evidence remains unknown; the reviewer must not invent context.
A fresh page timestamp cannot make old market evidence current.
Forming bars are not completed observations and cannot support a first review.
Finer bars relabelled as a larger interval are unusable evidence.
Missing transaction costs are unknown rather than a zero-cost pass.
Unspecified value per unit prevents a claim that position risk fits a dollar cap.
Unsupported strategy text must be surfaced as unassessed rather than interpreted as a known edge.
Known candle history cannot substitute for a stale executable quote when reviewing a position plan.
Prices without an attributable source must remain an evidence-quality unknown.
A learner cannot waive a known configured cap by writing a larger number into a hypothesis.
Existing account exposure remains relevant when a learner claims no existing risk.
Known realized loss cannot be erased by entering a zero loss assumption.
A claimed current closed-confirmation entry far away from all recent traded prices needs an entry-evidence concern rather than a numerical risk pass.
An explicitly structure-based target far outside all visible structure is not supported by that evidence, even when its reward multiple looks attractive.
The breakout method can support an observed completed boundary break when context and paper arithmetic are coherent.
A forecast or high wick is not a completed close beyond the observed boundary.
An explicitly pending breakout is unresolved information, not a falsely confirmed entry or an automatically defective future plan.
Evidence from a different instrument cannot support the learner hypothesis even if its trajectory agrees.
